title: Life Events
goal: Recognize the news someone shares and respond with celebration, a good wish, acknowledgment or sympathy.

study.title: Match the response to the news

runs.text: Some events are occasions for celebration. Others are difficult, mixed, or private. The speaker's own account helps you choose a response rather than assume how they feel.

rows.text: A graduation or promotion shared happily
Congratulations on the move. How are you settling in?
Wishing you all the best in your retirement.
I'm so sorry for your loss.

runs.text: Congrats
is a shortened informal form of
congratulations
Congratulations on...
names the achievement or event:
on your promotion
on graduating
on your new home
Good news at work
I got the promotion!
Congratulations! That's great news.

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: Thanks. I'm excited, but there's a lot to learn.

turns.en: Thanks. I'm excited, but there's a lot to learn.

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: I hope the first week goes well.

turns.en: I hope the first week goes well.

blocks.caption: Celebrate without taking over · Tess & Omar

runs.text: Tess has mixed feelings even while sharing good news. Omar responds to both the achievement and the new challenge.
I'm proud of you
expresses personal pride;
You worked hard for this
recognizes effort when you know that is true.
A birthday exchange

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: Happy birthday! Any plans for today?

turns.en: Happy birthday! Any plans for today?

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: Thanks. I'm having dinner with a couple of friends.

turns.en: Thanks. I'm having dinner with a couple of friends.

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: That sounds nice. Have a great evening.

turns.en: That sounds nice. Have a great evening.

blocks.caption: Celebrate without taking over · Omar & Tess

runs.text: The follow-up gives Tess room to say how she will celebrate. You do not need to ask someone's age or list the gifts they received.
At a new home
Welcome! We're still unpacking.

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: It's good to see your new place. How are you settling in?

turns.en: It's good to see your new place. How are you settling in?

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: Pretty well. The neighbors have been friendly.

turns.en: Pretty well. The neighbors have been friendly.

runs.text: I'm glad to hear that.

blocks.caption: Milestones and good wishes · Tess & Omar

runs.text: Settling in
means becoming familiar and comfortable in a new situation. A new home may be owned, rented or shared; the greeting does not need an ownership assumption.
For a wedding,
Congratulations to you both
addresses the couple. A short
Here's to Alex and River!
can begin a toast—a spoken good wish to people gathered for the occasion. A toast does not require this chapter to specify a particular drink.
A colleague's last day before retirement

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: Wishing you all the best in your retirement.

turns.en: Wishing you all the best in your retirement.

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: Thank you. I'll miss working with everyone.

turns.en: Thank you. I'll miss working with everyone.

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: We'll miss you too. I hope we stay in touch.

turns.en: We'll miss you too. I hope we stay in touch.

blocks.caption: Milestones and good wishes · Omar & Tess

runs.text: A good wish can acknowledge change without pretending the person has only one feeling.
Sympathy uses
sorry
differently from an apology, as Chapter 9 explained.
My aunt died last weekend.

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: I'm so sorry to hear that.

turns.en: I'm so sorry to hear that.

turns.speaker: Tess

runs.text: Thank you. I don't really want to talk about it yet.

turns.en: Thank you. I don't really want to talk about it yet.

turns.speaker: Omar

runs.text: Of course. We don't have to talk about it.

turns.en: Of course. We don't have to talk about it.

blocks.caption: Difficult or uncertain news · Tess & Omar

runs.text: For news such as a divorce or leaving a job, start with
How are you feeling about it?
if the feeling is unclear. If someone says
I'm relieved
I'm glad things are getting better for you
may fit. If they say
It's been really hard
, acknowledgment and support may fit better than congratulations. Chapter 19 develops offers of help.
Read each complete situation. On your own, say the news, your response, and the person's reply.
I passed my course! I'm so happy.
Celebrate. The speaker replies
Thanks. It was a lot of work
. Acknowledge the effort.
It is your friend's birthday. Wish them well and ask about plans. Their plan is dinner with friends.
A colleague says
I'm retiring next month. I'm excited, but I'll miss the team
. Give a good wish and acknowledge the second feeling.
My grandfather died. I don't want to discuss it right now.
Express sympathy and respect the stated preference.
The divorce is final.
No feeling is stated. Ask how they feel. Rehearse two continuations:
I'm relieved
and
I'm having a hard time
. Support:
I'm glad things are getting better
I'm sorry it's been so hard
Hide Study. Choose a life event and give a response that fits an invented speaker's feelings, rather than only the event label.
Sample possibilities
Congratulations! — Thanks. It was a lot of work. — You worked hard for this.
Happy birthday! Any plans for today? — Dinner with friends. — Have a great evening.
Wishing you all the best. We'll miss you too.
I'm so sorry for your loss. We don't have to talk about it.
How are you feeling about it?
followed by the fitting acknowledgment above.
Check:
Did your response fit the actual news and feeling? Did you avoid turning sympathy into an apology? Could you acknowledge both celebration and uncertainty without demanding private details?
